# seeNA

**Copy-number visualization in R, built for ichorCNA output.**

[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/bauernhofere/seeNA/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/bauernhofere/seeNA/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml?query=branch%3Amain)

Read your [ichorCNA](https://github.com/GavinHaLab/ichorCNA) results once and
move between genome-wide profiles, regional overlays, paired agreement tracks
and cohort heatmaps. seeNA handles genomic coordinates, sample annotations
and coverage while keeping the underlying measurements accessible.

- **Explore cohorts:** group and order samples by metadata, annotate rows,
  and display continuous signal or discrete CNA calls.
- **Compare samples:** align profiles on shared genomic coordinates and
  distinguish shared from sample-specific alterations.
- **Style your figures:** profiles return ggplot objects; heatmaps return
  ComplexHeatmap objects with controls for labels, legends and typography.

## Install

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("bauernhofere/seeNA")

# Additional dependencies for heatmaps:
install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install(c("ComplexHeatmap", "circlize"))
```

This is the GitHub development version. Record the installed commit with
`packageDescription("seeNA")$RemoteSha` for reproducible analyses.

## Try the examples

The gallery uses **24 synthetic samples** with 500 kb observations across
chromosomes 1–22 and X, three example groups, two timepoints and deliberately
missing intervals. The included, fixed-seed [generator](inst/examples/make-demo.R)
creates the input files in a temporary directory. These are demonstration data,
not patient data or fitted ichorCNA results.

```{r demo-data}
library(seeNA)
source(system.file("examples", "make-demo.R", package = "seeNA"))
manifest <- write_demo_cohort()
cohort <- read_ichor_cohort(manifest, genome_build = "hg38")
a <- cohort$samples[["demo-01"]]
b <- cohort$samples[["demo-02"]]
```

For your own data, provide a manifest with `sample_id`, `cna_seg`, optional
`seg` and `params` paths, and any sample annotations. Each row selects one
sample from one ichorCNA run. Paths can be relative to the manifest.

## Cohort landscapes

Show continuous segment-level signal on a shared genomic grid. Here, rows are
grouped by metadata and sorted by TF within each group; the side annotations
show timepoint and TF.

```{r matrix}
m <- ichor_matrix(
  cohort, value = "segment_median", bin_size = 1e6,
  chromosomes = c(as.character(1:22), "X")
)
meta <- m$samples
rows <- meta$sample_id[order(meta$group, -meta[["TF (%)"]])]
```

```{r heatmap, fig.width=11.5, fig.height=6.8, fig.alt="Continuous segment-median heatmap of 24 synthetic samples across chromosomes 1–22 and X. Three row groups have distinct alteration patterns; annotations show timepoint and specified TF. Grey cells mark missing intervals."}
h <- plot_ichor_heatmap(
  m, group = "group", row_order = rows,
  annotation_columns = c("timepoint", "TF (%)"),
  annotation_colors = list(
    timepoint = c(T1 = "#264653", T2 = "#E9C46A"),
    "TF (%)" = circlize::colorRamp2(c(0, 100), c("#F0F2F4", "#344955"))
  ),
  colors = circlize::colorRamp2(c(-1, 0, 1), c("#1E9E5E", "#FAFAFA", "#CB2B2B")),
  legend_title = "Segment median\nlog2 ratio",
  text_style = list(fontfamily = "sans", fontsize = 9),
  na_col = "#D5DADF"
)
missing_key <- ComplexHeatmap::Legend(
  title = "Coverage", labels = "Missing",
  legend_gp = grid::gpar(fill = "#D5DADF", col = NA)
)
ComplexHeatmap::draw(
  h, heatmap_legend_list = list(missing_key),
  column_title = "Cohort landscape | synthetic examples",
  column_title_gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 14, fontface = "bold")
)
```

The color scale is shared across rows; grey marks missing coverage. Segment
medians retain continuous logR amplitude, which reflects TF as well as copy-number
change. Their coverage describes segment spans, rather than individual observed
bins. The ±1 color endpoints above set display saturation, not calling thresholds.

Choose the measurement that answers your question:

| `value` | Measurement |
|---|---|
| `"segment_median"` | Exported segment log2 ratios, overlap-weighted onto the grid |
| `"logR"` | Bin-level log2 ratios |
| `"call"` | Discrete CNA categories; corrected calls by default |
| `"copy_number"` / `"corrected_copy_number"` | Corresponding exported copy-number values |

For a call landscape, change the matrix `value` to `"call"` and use the heatmap's
default categorical palette. `m$coverage` and `m$mixed` expose the supporting
coverage and mixed-call flags. Factor levels set group order; `row_order` sets
order within each block.

## Genome-wide profiles

Display the original bin-level logR values, call colors and segment medians
on reference-length chromosome axes.

```{r profile, fig.height=3.8, fig.alt="Genome-wide profile of a synthetic sample with thousands of half-megabase observations, broad and focal alterations, grey segment medians, and chromosome boundaries."}
plot_ichor_profile(a, point_size = 0.45) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Genome-wide copy-number profile",
    subtitle = "Synthetic demo-01 | hg38 | 500 kb observations"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom", axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 7))
```

To read a single sample directly:

```{r single-sample, eval=FALSE}
sample <- read_ichor_sample(
  "sample.cna.seg", seg = "sample.seg", params = "sample.params.txt",
  genome_build = "hg38"
)
plot_ichor_profile(sample)
```

## Regional comparisons

Overlay samples at any chromosome or `chr:start-end` interval. Points retain
their original genomic positions, and segments retain their source medians.

```{r region, fig.height=3.8, fig.alt="Two synthetic profiles across chromosome 1 with hundreds of original bin observations, shared gains, sample-specific changes, opposite-direction calls and a missing interval."}
plot_ichor_region(
  list(a, b), "chr1:1-240000000", point_size = 0.8,
  colors = c("demo-01" = "#007A87", "demo-02" = "#B36B28")
) + ggplot2::labs(
  title = "Compare the same genomic region",
  subtitle = "Synthetic pair | original bins and segment medians"
) + ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Use `plot_ichor_compare(list(a, b))` for the genome-wide overlay.

## Shared and sample-specific alterations

Add a directional agreement track beneath a pair of profiles. The track
separates one-sided changes, shared directions and opposite directions on a
common grid. It compares **CNA calls**; bar heights show the samples' logR.

```{r concordance, fig.width=10, fig.height=5.5, fig.alt="Two synthetic chromosome-1 profiles above a paired agreement track showing shared gain, A-only loss, B-only gain, opposite directions and unknown coverage in a deliberately missing interval."}
plot_ichor_concordance(
  a, b, region = "chr1:1-240000000", bin_size = 1e6,
  sample_labels = c("A", "B"), point_size = 0.65,
  ylim = c(-1, 1), show_sample_id = FALSE
) + ggplot2::labs(
  title = "Shared and sample-specific alterations",
  subtitle = "Synthetic pair | 1 Mb comparison grid"
)
```

The default track shows each altered sample in its half of the target bin.
`height = "representative"` provides a single-height summary. Retrieve the
underlying comparison with `ichor_pair_concordance(a, b)`.

## Styling and reproducibility

Use ggplot themes, labels and `ggsave()` for profiles and comparisons. Heatmaps
support `group`, `row_order`, `row_labels`, `text_style` and custom palettes;
render them with `ComplexHeatmap::draw()` on your chosen graphics device.
Hide identifiers with `show_sample_id = FALSE` or `show_row_names = FALSE`.

Raw logR is the default. Set `ploidy_adjust = TRUE` on profile/comparison plots
to apply ichorCNA's mixture-ploidy display shift. It is distinct from purity
correction. Public helpers expose TF, ploidy, reference coordinates and input
provenance:

```{r helpers, eval=FALSE}
ichor_tf(a)
ichor_ploidy(a)
ichor_genome_layout("hg38")
ichor_provenance(cohort)
sessionInfo()
```

## Development

```bash
make bootstrap  # install development dependencies
make readme     # rebuild this page and its gallery
make test
make check
```

CI checks Linux, macOS and Windows, including ggplot2 3.5 compatibility.
Contribution and scientific-contract guidance lives in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).
